reasoning: Counterexample at n = 5: 2^(2^5) + 1 = 2^32 + 1 = 4294967297. This factors as 641 × 6700417: 641 × 6700417 = 641 × 6,700,000 + 641 × 417 = 4,294,700,000 + 267,297 = 4,294,967,297. Verification that 641 | 2^32 + 1: 641 = 5^4 + 2^4 = 5·2^7 + 1. From 5·2^7 ≡ -1 (mod 641), raising to the 4th power gives 5^4·2^28 ≡ 1 (mod 641). Since 5^4 ≡ -2^4 (mod 641), substituting yields -2^4·2^28 = -2^32 ≡ 1 (mod 641), i.e. 2^32 + 1 ≡ 0 (mod 641). Hence F_5 is composite (Euler, 1732), so the claim fails. (F_0..F_4 = 3, 5, 17, 257, 65537 are prime, but no Fermat prime beyond F_4 is known.)
